content:
A greenhouse insurance enquiry should separate the structure, covering, technical installations and crop. Damage to a frame, a failed heating unit and spoiled plants are not one interchangeable loss. For growers in Moldova planning 2027 production, this separation helps identify which costs remain with the farm and which could be considered under an actual policy.

Editorial revision: 26 November 2026. Planning material for 2027; the scenarios below are hypothetical, not incident or demand forecasts.

Who needs a separate greenhouse file?

The assessment is relevant to vegetable and seedling growers, nursery operators and businesses extending existing protected cultivation. Describe permanent greenhouses and seasonal polytunnels individually. A lightweight tunnel and a heated installation with automated ventilation should not share an unexplained total value.

List the frame, glass or film, heating, ventilation, irrigation, controls and movable equipment. Describe the pumps and distribution through a separate irrigation-equipment inventory rather than counting the same component twice. Identify owners, lessees and contractors. Keep crop value separate from the cost of the building and installations, including when the same financing agreement covers both.

Which risks should be discussed?

Prepare specific questions about wind, hail, snow loading, fire and accidental damage to equipment. MOLDASIG's agricultural information mentions greenhouses and tunnels among equipment categories (checked 25 November 2026). It confirms a published category, not acceptance of this structure or crop.

Ask whether the actual conditions exclude or limit wear of covering, known structural defects, maintenance shortcomings, crop disease or consequences of a heating failure. These are matters to clarify, not a universal list of exclusions. Do not infer the answer from the phrase agricultural insurance.

Planning for the 2027 season

Use a hypothetical operational exercise: a heating problem develops overnight while seedlings are present. Identify who receives an alert, who can intervene safely and which alternative is technically available. This is not a prediction of cold weather or a statement that insurance pays the plants' value.

Before adding another tunnel, update the declared area, construction type and equipment schedule. Compare crop stages with the periods proposed by the insurer. A summer structure inventory does not fully describe the winter use of a heated greenhouse.

Prevention should follow the real structure

Have competent people review the condition of the frame and covering, outstanding heating or ventilation faults and the arrangements for receiving alerts. Document repairs and remaining recommendations before the next crop cycle. A polytunnel photograph or the existence of a sensor does not establish structural safety or a working response process.

What determines the premium?

No verified premium for your 2027 greenhouse is available in this article. Insurers need the construction, location, documented values, crops or equipment being considered, operating season and requested events. The premium is the amount paid for insurance; the deductible is the insured's retained part of a loss under the contract. (BNM: contract terms, checked 25 November 2026; general guidance, not individual policy conditions.)

Check valuation carefully. Replacing a covering is different from rebuilding the structure, and investment cost is not automatically the value of a crop. Compare proposals on the same basis and ask how removal, access, labour and reinstallation expenses are treated.

Documents and responsibilities

Prepare ownership or use documents, technical records, construction and equipment invoices, maintenance history and available acceptance records. For plants, organize crop type, planting periods, areas and the proposed value basis. Do not replace missing agronomic information with assumed yields.

If financial support is relevant, consult AIPA's agricultural-insurance information, checked on 25 November 2026, and verify the rules for the applicable season. A support mechanism described today does not establish the amount, eligibility or payment date of a 2027 subsidy.

Three situations: what to compare before deciding

The MOLDASIG equipment list, rechecked on 26 November 2026, includes greenhouses and tunnels. It does not establish acceptance of every covering, crop or heating-related loss.

  • Structure or covering damaged: compare the frame, covering, installations and crop separately. Prepare the inventory, age and values. Check named items and causes rather than adding crop value to a structure entry without agreement.
  • Heating stops with the structure intact: compare equipment findings with agronomic consequences. Retain maintenance records and dated crop observations. Ask whether each event and consequence is addressed; a temperature change does not alone identify an insured cause.
  • New tunnel or planting cycle in 2027: compare area, crop and period with the previous schedule. Prepare updated plans and supported values. Verify the change procedure and accepted dates instead of carrying forward an outdated seasonal description.

Frequently asked questions

What determines the cost of greenhouse insurance?

Describe the construction, covering, equipment, location, season and requested risks, with values for structures and crops separately. Read deductibles and expense limits using the same inventory version. A proposal for an unheated tunnel should not be compared directly with one considering heated structures, technical installations and a different operating period.

What records should the grower prepare?

Organize ownership or use documents, construction and equipment invoices, technical and acceptance records, maintenance and known defects. For plants, retain the crop type, planting periods, areas and proposed value basis. Do not replace missing agronomic evidence with assumed yields, and ask what additional records the actual assessment requires.

What should be recorded after storm damage or a heating problem?

Put safety, competent intervention and necessary crop-protection decisions first. Where safe, retain the discovery time, affected structure or equipment, observations and relevant service findings. Notify according to the actual policy and request evidence instructions. Do not enter an unsafe structure for photographs or assume that every subsequent crop expense is accepted.

Does insurance for the frame include plants and heating equipment?

Check the objects expressly identified. The frame, covering, installations and plants need their own description and value basis. Ask how a technical failure and its effects on crops are treated. Being located inside an insured greenhouse does not by itself establish that every item or consequence is included.

How is worn covering distinguished from accidental damage?

Retain condition and maintenance records, the observation timeline and competent findings about the cause. Ask how the proposal defines wear, sudden damage and any relevant limitations. A newly noticed tear is not proof that all deterioration arose that day, while an old covering does not alone determine the insurer decision.
